public_rationale: The claim has a cause and an effect. The effect partly holds. Harvey raised $160M in December 2025, $200M in March 2026 and $550M in September 2026, so it did raise hundreds of millions every few months. Perplexity did not: a Reuters report from August 2026 says its last financing was about a year earlier, and a new round was only in talks. The cause is the core claim: that these firms resell lab tokens at a loss and that this forces the raises. No reliable public source reports either company's gross margin or model costs against revenue, and no source ties the raises to serving losses. Harvey's own deal note points to its work on its own model. Without margin data the causal claim can't be confirmed or refuted.
limitations: Private-company financials are not public, and margin estimates online are unsourced.
The fundraising evidence covers only the two named companies, not wrapper startups in general.
Funding cadence alone can't show why a company raises.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI startups that are wrappers built on Anthropic's and OpenAI's models are fundamentally built on reselling the labs' tokens at a loss, which is why companies like Harvey and Perplexity must raise hundreds of millions of dollars every few months.
conditions: wrapper businesses built on the labs' models

statement.excerpt: These businesses are fundamentally built on reselling tokens from the large AI labs at a loss, which is why companies like Harvey and Perplexity have to raise hundreds of millions of dollars every few months.

from_speaker: businesses are fundamentally built on reselling tokens from the large AI labs
have to raise hundreds of millions of dollars
our_interpretation: Plain reading: wrapper startups such as Harvey and Perplexity pay the labs more for model usage (tokens) than they earn from customers for it, so they lose money on serving. That loss is the reason they must keep raising large rounds often.

Three parts must hold: (1) a loss on reselling model output, meaning negative gross margin or serving costs above revenue; (2) Harvey and Perplexity each raise hundreds of millions of dollars at intervals of a few months; (3) the losses are what force the raises.
He describes an ongoing state with no period named. I use the year before the post (2025-09-01 to 2026-09-29) as the period public evidence could cover.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports show negative gross margins or serving costs above revenue at Harvey and Perplexity (or wrapper startups broadly), and both firms raising hundreds of millions of dollars every few months to cover those losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports show these firms have positive gross margins on serving customers, or that they do not raise hundreds of millions every few months, or that they raise for reasons other than covering losses on serving.

evidence.excerpt: Today, Harvey announced a $160M investment at an $8B valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz.
evidence.explanation: One of a run of Harvey rounds in the hundreds of millions a few months apart. It supports the fundraising-cadence part only, not the loss-on-tokens cause.

evidence.excerpt: Harvey, a startup that develops artificial intelligence for law firms, has raised $200 million in a new funding round that values the company at $11 billion.
evidence.explanation: A second Harvey raise about three and a half months after December 2025. This fits 'hundreds of millions every few months' for Harvey.

evidence.excerpt: Harvey has announced a US$550 million funding round at a US$15.5 billion valuation, co-led by Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners. The raise follows the introduction of Harvey’s first post-trained open-weight model
evidence.explanation: A third large Harvey raise about six months later, which supports the cadence. It also shows Harvey putting out its own post-trained model, which cuts slightly against a pure 'token reseller' picture. It says nothing about margins.

evidence.excerpt: The Information reported in September last year that Perplexity had finalized a $20 billion valuation.
evidence.explanation: The same Reuters report calls Perplexity's previous financing 'a year ago' and says a new Nvidia round was only in talks. So in the year before the post, Perplexity did not raise every few months.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reliable reporting or filings (for example IPO prospectuses or leaked financials reported by The Information or Reuters) showing Harvey's and Perplexity's gross margins and model costs against revenue, plus any statement of why they raised.
